provenance: Hand-built offline prototype, 2026-07-26. Claims were written by reading the article-level fields already present in the 2026-07-11 snapshot (id, url, publisher, publishedAt, title) for three existing clusters: 12 politics, 18 world, 13 business. No model-generated summary, P/H composite, or lean score was treated as evidence, and no article text is reproduced. This file is authored review material, not pipeline output, and is not regenerated by scripts/refresh.sh.

receipts.claim: Graham Platner filed paperwork to withdraw from the Maine Senate race.

sources.supports: Reports the withdrawal as filed, not merely announced.
Independently reports the ballot-withdrawal filing.
Third outlet, different lean, same underlying event.

receipts.claim: Maine Democrats must name a replacement nominee by July 27.

sources.supports: Carries the July 27 replacement date.
Independently carries the same convention deadline.

receipts.claim: Whether Platner committed the assault a former partner alleges.

positions.statement: A former partner has accused Platner of rape, and outlets across the spectrum report the accusation as the trigger for his exit.

sources.supports: Reports the former girlfriend's allegation.
Independently reports the allegation preceding the withdrawal.

positions.statement: Platner denies the allegation and attributes his exit to collapsed fundraising and establishment pressure.

sources.supports: Records the denial and his stated reasons for leaving.

receipts.claim: What the withdrawal means for who wins the Maine seat.

sources.supports: Analyst commentary on the race. Paywalled video: linked, not reproduced.
Forecasts midterm consequences.

receipts.note: Both sources offer forecasting and analysis, not a reportable fact. LITMUS records this as unresolved rather than scoring a prediction.

receipts.claim: The United States has demanded Iran publicly state that the Strait of Hormuz is open to commercial shipping.

sources.supports: Reports the demand and the commitment sought on commercial vessels.
Independently reports the same demand.

receipts.claim: Commercial traffic through the Strait of Hormuz has fallen sharply.

sources.supports: Reports a significant fall in strait traffic.
Independently reports disrupted shipping through the strait.

receipts.claim: Which side ended the memorandum that paused the fighting.

positions.statement: The U.S. account: Iran violated the memorandum by attacking commercial vessels, and the administration treats the ceasefire as over.

sources.supports: Reports the violation claim as the stated basis for the demand.
Reports the ceasefire declared ended over vessel attacks.

positions.statement: A competing account: the U.S. itself stepped away from the memorandum, leaving the interim deal's status uncertain.

sources.supports: Describes a U.S. withdrawal from the memorandum and an uncertain deal.

receipts.claim: The deadline given to Iran falls on Saturday.

sources.supports: The only outlet in this cluster naming a specific deadline day.

receipts.note: One outlet in this edition carries the specific deadline. That is below the bar for confirmed, so it stands unverified here.

receipts.claim: Apple has sued OpenAI in federal court alleging theft of trade secrets.

sources.supports: Reports the federal filing and its trade-secret allegations.
Independently reports the complaint.
Third independent account of the same filing.

receipts.claim: The complaint names former Apple hardware executive Tang Tan, now at OpenAI.

sources.supports: Names Tan as a defendant and a long-tenured Apple veteran.
Independently names Tan among the former employees at issue.

receipts.claim: Whether OpenAI in fact took Apple trade secrets.

positions.statement: Apple's position, as filed: OpenAI solicited and obtained confidential Apple material through departing employees and job candidates.

sources.supports: Reports Apple's characterization of the alleged scheme.
Independently reports the solicitation allegations and named individuals.

positions.statement: OpenAI denies the allegations and says it is reviewing the filing.

sources.supports: Carries OpenAI's own responsive statement.

receipts.claim: The suit follows a cooling of the 2024 Apple-OpenAI partnership after OpenAI's acquisition of Jony Ive's hardware startup.

sources.supports: The only source in this cluster supplying the partnership and acquisition background.

receipts.note: Only one outlet in this edition supplies this background, so it is presented as unverified context rather than an established fact.
